subject: Chemistry
topic: Oxidation, reduction and redox — mixed tiers
description: Definitions, oxidising/reducing agents, electrochemical cells, common redox examples

questions.stem: In a chemical reaction, OXIDATION is best defined as:

options.option_text: Loss of electrons (or gain of oxygen)

questions.explanation: Modern definition: oxidation = loss of electrons; reduction = gain of electrons (mnemonic OIL RIG — Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain). Older definitions: oxidation = gain of oxygen / loss of hydrogen / increase in oxidation number. Reduction = loss of oxygen / gain of hydrogen / decrease in oxidation number. The two always occur together = REDOX. Example: Mg + ½O₂ → MgO; Mg loses 2e⁻ (oxidised), O₂ gains 2e⁻ (reduced).

questions.stem: In the reaction Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu, the oxidising agent is:
questions.explanation: Oxidising agent = species that ITSELF gets reduced (i.e. it OXIDISES the other). Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu (reduction; Cu²⁺ is oxidised — wait, reduced) — so Cu²⁺ is the OXIDISING AGENT. Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻ (oxidation; Zn loses electrons) — so Zn is the REDUCING AGENT. SO₄²⁻ is just a spectator ion (unchanged). Trick: 'oxidising agent' is read 'agent that causes oxidation' = it accepts electrons.

questions.stem: The 'rusting' of iron is essentially an example of:

options.option_text: Slow electrochemical oxidation in presence of moisture and oxygen

questions.explanation: Rust = hydrated iron(III) oxide (Fe₂O₃ · xH₂O), reddish-brown. Mechanism — galvanic micro-cells form on the iron surface; Fe loses electrons (anode: Fe → Fe²⁺ + 2e⁻); oxygen + water consume them (cathode: O₂ + 2H₂O + 4e⁻ → 4OH⁻); Fe²⁺ then oxidises further to Fe³⁺ and combines with hydroxide and water → rust. Prevention: galvanising (zinc coating, sacrificial anode), painting, alloying (stainless steel = Fe + Cr + Ni). Salt water accelerates rusting (electrolyte improves the cell).

questions.stem: The oxidation number of sulphur in H₂SO₄ is:
questions.explanation: Sum of oxidation numbers in a neutral compound = 0. H₂SO₄ has 2 H (+1 each = +2), 4 O (−2 each = −8), and S = x. Equation: 2 + x − 8 = 0 → x = +6. So S is in +6 oxidation state in H₂SO₄. Other common S states: −2 (H₂S), 0 (S₈ elemental), +2 (S₂Cl₂), +4 (SO₂, H₂SO₃), +6 (SO₃, H₂SO₄). The +6 state is the highest oxidation number S can show.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a strong REDUCING agent?
questions.explanation: Reducing agent = donates electrons → gets oxidised. H₂ readily donates: H₂ → 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ (used in metal extraction: WO₃ + 3H₂ → W + 3H₂O). F₂ is the strongest OXIDISING agent (most electronegative). Cl₂ and O₂ are also oxidising agents. Other reducing agents: alkali metals (Na, K), CO, H₂S, SO₂, hydrogen sulphite, ascorbic acid, NaBH₄ (mild). In organic chemistry: LiAlH₄ (very strong), DIBAL-H, Zn-Hg/HCl (Clemmensen), Zn/HOAc.

questions.stem: In a galvanic (voltaic) cell, oxidation occurs at the:
questions.explanation: Galvanic / voltaic cell — converts chemical energy → electrical energy spontaneously. Anode = oxidation site (loses electrons, called negative terminal because electrons leave). Cathode = reduction site (gains electrons, positive terminal). Mnemonic 'AN OX, RED CAT' — Anode Oxidation, Reduction Cathode. NOTE: in ELECTROLYTIC cells, signs reverse — anode is positive (electrons forced out by external supply) and cathode is negative. Daniell cell — Zn/Zn²⁺ || Cu²⁺/Cu, EMF = +1.10 V.

questions.stem: The browning of cut apples is best classified as a:
questions.explanation: When an apple is cut, polyphenol oxidase (PPO) enzymes inside cells contact atmospheric O₂; they catalyse oxidation of phenolic compounds to brown quinones — hence the browning. Slowed by: refrigeration, dipping in lemon juice (vitamin C is a reducing agent — competes for O₂), salt water, blanching (heat denatures enzyme). Same mechanism: browning of bananas, potatoes, mushrooms. Genetically engineered 'Arctic apple' has the PPO gene silenced — does not brown when cut.
